# BioManager user guide

> BioManager is a free, open-source lab management app for a biology lab's animal colonies (mice, zebrafish, flies, worms and any other organism), plasmids, samples, orders, reagents, antibodies and viruses, with a calendar and a lab notebook. Website: https://biomanager.org. This file is the whole English user guide (https://biomanager.org/guide) in one place, followed by the guide to deploying a lab server; the Chinese guide is at https://biomanager.org/zh/guide.

---

## Using BioManager

Everything BioManager does, and how to move a lab into it: from a first launch to a whole lab on a shared server.

### Your first day

Six steps, in order. New here, or coming from spreadsheets? Read [Coming from Excel](https://biomanager.org/guide/coming-from-excel) first: it takes ten minutes and saves you days.

1. [**Install BioManager**: Download, unzip and open it. On a Mac, right-click → Open the first time. (2 min)](https://biomanager.org/guide/install)

2. [**Set up your lab**: Create the first account, which is the admin, and tick what your lab keeps. (3 min)](https://biomanager.org/guide/install#first-run)

3. [**Bring your lab in from Excel**: Import a sheet, and check the preview before anything is saved. (10 min)](https://biomanager.org/guide/import-from-excel)

4. [**Work in a sheet**: Edit in place, fill down, sort and filter. (5 min)](https://biomanager.org/guide/sheets)

5. [**Find anything**: Search everything with `⌘` `K`. (2 min)](https://biomanager.org/guide/finding-things)

6. [**Invite your lab**: Approve sign-ups in Settings → People & access, or give a visitor a guest pass. (5 min)](https://biomanager.org/guide/invite-someone)

### Find your way

Or search the whole guide: press `/` or `⌘` `K`.

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide

---

## What BioManager is

What BioManager keeps for a lab, and how it differs from a spreadsheet.

BioManager is one place for what a biology lab keeps: animals (mice, zebrafish, flies, worms, or any organism you describe), plasmids, samples, orders, reagents, antibodies and viruses, with a calendar and a notebook beside them. It looks and edits like a spreadsheet, but underneath it is a database that understands your lab: it knows a mouse lives in a cage on a rack, that a litter born today is weaned at P21, that a vial at 18 °C is flipped half as often as at 25 °C, and that an antibody expires next month.

It comes in two forms, the same program in both:

| Desktop app | For one person. macOS, Windows or Linux; your data stays on your computer. |
|---|---|
| Lab server | For a whole lab: one BioManager that everyone opens in a browser, the Android app, or from an iPhone's home screen. Usually free to host. [Every way to run one.](https://biomanager.org/server) The desktop app can set one up for you: **Settings → Devices & copies → Set up a lab server** asks where it should go, does the work, and can bring your records along. |

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/what-it-is

---

## Coming from Excel

How your spreadsheets map onto BioManager, and what to do with each one.

If your lab runs on spreadsheets, you already know most of BioManager. The sheet is still there — click a cell and type — but each thing Excel makes you do by hand, BioManager does for you.

#### What you know, and what it becomes

| In Excel | In BioManager |
|---|---|
| A workbook with a tab per thing | Your lab, with a **database** per thing in the sidebar: Mouse, Fish, Plasmids, Orders… |
| A row | A **record** with a number that is never reused, so "mouse 1042" means one mouse forever. |
| Typing, then Save, then "who has the file open?" | Type in the cell; it **saves as you type**. Everyone edits the same records at once, and nobody's work overwrites anyone else's. |
| AutoFilter | The search box and the **chips** above every sheet: *All, Alive, Mine*, one per status. Your last choice is remembered, and it is in the page's address, so a bookmark or a link you send opens the sheet the same way. |
| Freeze panes, hide columns, column widths | The ID stays pinned as you scroll; **Columns** hides and shows; drag a column's edge to resize. Remembered per sheet. |
| Data validation drop-downs | **Choices** for a column (statuses, categories, purposes), set in **Configure** or **Dropdowns**. Renaming one renames it everywhere. |
| Autocomplete from the column | **Suggestions** from everything the lab typed before. In inventories, picking an earlier item fills in its vendor, catalogue number and price. |
| Fill down, copy a row | In the mice's **Add many** preview, click a cell and **Fill down** (or `Ctrl`/`⌘` + `D`) copies it to the rows below. **Duplicate** copies any record. |
| Paste a column | Copy a column of readings (a Nanodrop export, say) or a block of cells, click the first cell in the sheet and paste: the values go down the rows as shown, and across if you copied several columns, each saved as if typed. A number steps over a choice column it isn't one of (the unit between concentration and A260/280), and a note says which rows it went into, first to last, so a list in another order shows at once. |
| Formulas for age, wean and flip dates | Worked out for you: ages, P21 weaning, genotyping dates, flip schedules that follow the incubator's temperature. |
| Conditional formatting | Status pills, a dot for what is alive or in use (coloured by age for animals), expired stock in red — and the **Home** page gathering everything that needs you today. |
| VLOOKUP between sheets | Real links: a mouse is in a cage on a rack; a sample came from that mouse; an order became that reagent. Click through. |
| Version history, "who changed this?" | The **Audit log** records every edit, who made it and what it was before; **Batch history** undoes any bulk change. |
| Mail-merge for cage labels | **Cage cards** sized for card stock, each with a QR code that opens the cage on a phone. |
| Your old workbook | **Import from Excel** on every database reads it as it is, whatever its columns are called. |
| Save As CSV | **Export** on every sheet (CSV; for mice also Excel and PDF). Your data is never locked in. |

Once BioManager is installed and the lab is set up, [bring your sheets in](https://biomanager.org/guide/bring-your-lab-in): about half an hour.

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/coming-from-excel

---

## Install and set up

Install the desktop app, open it the first time, and set up your lab.

#### Get it

| macOS | [Download](https://biomanager.org/download), unzip, drag **BioManager** into Applications. The first time, **right-click it → Open**, then Open. |
|---|---|
| Windows | Extract the zip, open the **BioManager** folder, run **BioManager.exe**. At the warning choose **More info → Run anyway**. Its window uses Microsoft Edge WebView2, which Windows 11 has; on a Windows 10 PC without it, BioManager offers to download it from Microsoft and opens in your web browser meanwhile. Install it, then open BioManager again for its own window. |
| Linux | Mark `BioManager-Linux.AppImage` executable (right-click → Properties, or `chmod +x`) and open it. |
| Updates | The desktop app checks for a new version once a day and offers it, with what's new; **BioManager → Check for Updates…** (on Windows and Linux, **Help**) asks now. **Install and Restart** downloads it, checks it, and swaps it in as the app quits; where it can't (the Linux `.tar.gz`, a folder it can't write to), it opens the download to install as above. Your data stays where it is, and before a new version changes it a copy is kept ([Your data](https://biomanager.org/guide/your-data)). Turn the daily check off with **Check for Updates Automatically**. |
| What's new | After an update, on a desktop or a lab server, the first page you open shows a short **What's new**: what is new, what works differently and what was fixed, with a link to the full notes. **Got it** closes it for good; **Help → What's new** opens it again. |
| A lab server | Nothing to install: open the address your admin gives you. It opens on your lab's sign-in, with its name and what it keeps; new to the lab, choose **Ask to join**. Setting one up is on [Run it for your lab](https://biomanager.org/server). |
| Updating a lab server | The server looks for a new version once a day and tells its admins. They find it in **Settings → Version**, with what's new and a link to the release notes. **Update now** takes a backup, installs the new version and restarts the server; BioManager is away for a minute or two, and the page comes back by itself on the new version. The phone apps open the server, so they follow it. Turn the daily look off with **Check for new versions every day**. |
| Phones | The Android app, or your lab server added to an iPhone's home screen: see [Phones and cage cards](https://biomanager.org/guide/phones-and-cage-cards). |

> **Why the warning on a computer?** The apps aren't signed by Apple or Microsoft, so the system asks you to confirm once per version.

#### Starting a lab

The first time the desktop app opens, it asks **Does your lab already use BioManager?** **Yes, open my lab** takes the lab's address, then you sign in as you do at the lab (or **use a code** approved on a device already signed in), and the computer joins the lab as one of your devices: its window works on the lab from then on, and it keeps a copy for when the server can't be reached ([Your devices](https://biomanager.org/guide/your-data#your-devices)). Nothing is made on the computer. **No, start a new lab** makes a new, empty lab, and says so: you name it, choose whether it lives on this computer or a lab server, and make its first account, which is the lab's **admin**. A server nobody has set up says it has no lab yet, and starts the same way, with the one-time setup code printed when the server started. The admin then answers a short survey, and BioManager builds exactly what you'll use — nothing more:

1. **Your lab** — its name, time zone, how dates are written, and the weaning and genotyping days ([what these do](https://biomanager.org/guide/lab-setup)).

2. **What does your lab keep?** Tick animals and stocks (mice, zebrafish, flies, worms, other organisms) and molecular and supplies (plasmids, samples, orders, reagents, chemicals, antibodies, viruses). For each, a little more: a name (e.g. *Mouse room B*); for the colony how many racks, their size and how positions are labelled; for flies and worms which incubator temperatures you run. Blank means the usual.

3. **Which lab functions?** The calendar and the notebook.

4. **What may members do?** Whether members may create databases of their own, whether they may add databases for the whole lab, whether they may keep a copy of the lab on their computers, and whether they may make [API tokens](https://biomanager.org/guide/scripts-and-api).

Below the questions, a note says BioManager sends its makers a few anonymous counts once a day, which helps keep it free and going ([what is sent](https://biomanager.org/guide/your-data#counts)). To stop them, switch off **Share anonymous counts with BioManager's makers** in **Settings → General**, then or any time later.

BioManager then makes those databases, the racks and incubators too, and shows the lab ready, with the address people join at. Everyone who joins later gets a one-page welcome tour of the lab's databases on first sign-in (**Settings → Your data → See the welcome tour again** brings it back).

**English or 中文.** BioManager shows in the language your computer or browser asks for first, English or Simplified Chinese; the desktop app follows your computer's. Choose for yourself under **Settings → Appearance & language**, which changes as soon as you pick, or with the **中文 / English** switch on the sign-in page, which then stays your choice when you sign in. Everyone in the lab chooses their own; names, notes and everything people type stay as written.

**Easier to read.** Text is set in Inter, which tells I, l and 1 apart in IDs and genotypes, with your computer's own Chinese font. **Settings → Appearance & language → Font** switches to the computer's font instead (SF Pro on a Mac, Segoe UI on Windows). **Text size** there makes everything smaller or larger in the Mac app; in a browser, its zoom does the same (`⌘` `+` and `⌘` `−`, or `Ctrl` on Windows).

### Troubleshooting

#### The app won't open on my Mac

Right-click it and choose **Open**. If macOS says it's damaged, move it to Applications first, then try again.

#### Linux: the AppImage does nothing

Mark it executable. If it still won't start, install `libfuse2`, or use the `.tar.gz` and run `BioManager/BioManager`.

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/install

---

## Try it first

Ten minutes on a practice rack: make a cage, add mice, record a litter, and watch the weaning date appear. Then throw it away.

Who and where: Anyone, in a new lab · Desktop and lab server

Before you move a real colony in, it is worth seeing the whole loop once on records that do not matter. Everything below is made in your own lab and deleted at the end, so nothing you do here can spoil anything. If a step does not look like this page says, that is worth telling us — the guide is meant to match the app.

### 1. A practice rack

1. Open **Mouse** in the sidebar, then the **Cages** tab.

2. **Rack grid → New rack**. Call it *Practice*, 2 rows by 3 columns, and save.

An empty grid of six positions appears, labelled the way you chose — the same grid every rack in the lab uses.

### 2. A cage with mice in it

1. **New cage**. Put it in the *Practice* rack at the first position, and set **Purpose** to *Breeding*.

2. Open the cage and add two mice: one female, one male. Give them any genotype you like.

The cage shows 2 mice, and its card sits in the first square of the rack. The mice are yours: your name is on them.

### 3. A litter, and the dates that follow

1. On the cage, press **Litter born** and keep today's date.

2. Press **Record the litter**.

BioManager says *Recorded a litter born today in cage … : weaning is due …* — three weeks out. You did not work that date out, and neither will anyone else in the lab. Open [Home](https://biomanager.org/guide/home-page) and the [calendar](https://biomanager.org/guide/calendar): the weaning is waiting there on the day it is due, in both places, because they are the same list.

### 4. Throw it away

1. Open **Settings → History** and **Undo** what you just made, newest first.

2. Anything left: delete the mice, then the cage, then the rack in **Rack grid**.

The colony is empty again and ready for your real records. Nothing was sent anywhere while you did this — see [Your data and backups](https://biomanager.org/guide/your-data).

Next: [Bring your lab in](https://biomanager.org/guide/bring-your-lab-in) moves your real records across, and [Coming from Excel](https://biomanager.org/guide/coming-from-excel) explains what changes when a sheet becomes a database.

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/try-it-first

---

## Bring your lab in

Move your records in: import sheets, add many at once, and check what came in.

About half an hour, once the lab is set up. There are two ways in: **Import from Excel** for the sheets you already keep, and **Add many** for a new group you describe once.

1. **Make your racks first.** **Cages → Rack grid → New rack**, named as in your sheet and labelled like the stickers on the real racks. Then a sheet with *Rack* and *Position* columns puts every cage in its place; anything without a position waits in *Unplaced* for you to drag on (on a tablet: **Move**, tap the cage, tap its place).

2. **Open Import from Excel.** Every database has it under **•••** in the toolbar above its sheet — Mice, Fish, Plasmids, fly and worm vials, any organism and every inventory. **Choose a file** (`.xlsx`, CSV or TSV, up to 15 MB and 5,000 rows) and press **Continue**. If the workbook has several sheets, pick one above the matches. No template, no renaming columns.

3. **Check how the columns were matched.** BioManager matches by meaning, not just by name: *Position*, *Slot* and *Well* are the position, *DOB* and *Born* the date of birth, *Supplier* the vendor, *Cat. No.* the catalogue number. Where a name could mean two things the values decide — a *Location* of `A1`, `B2`… is a position in a box, one of `Freezer 2` is a location. Headers in Chinese count too (*性别*, *出生日期*, *笼号*, *质粒名称*), in a CSV saved by Excel on a Chinese Windows as well. Each match says why; change any of them.

4. **Nothing is lost unless you say so.** A column BioManager doesn't have becomes a new column in an inventory or organism database (if you may configure it), or goes **Into the notes** as `Header: value`; choose **Leave out** to skip it. A must-have column your sheet lacks, like the owner, gets one value for every row — for plasmids and stock, also whether every row is *Personal* or *Lab common* (a *Lab common* column says it row by row). Dates stay as Excel wrote them (`3/14/2026`, `14/03/2026`, `12-May-26`): each column decides whether day or month comes first, and when it can't tell, the lab's date style (**Settings → General**) does. A date that can't be read, or a birth date in the future, is left blank and kept in the notes. *Male*, *m*, *♂* and *公* all become M; statuses and people are matched by name, and a plasmid's `152.6 ng/µl` is its concentration. A *Cage #* typed once and merged down over its mice counts for each of them. Typed once with blank cells below instead, a cage, rack, box or tank column offers **Its blank cells take the value above them**, ticked; untick it if a blank means none. The cages the import makes belong to their mice's owner.

5. **Preview, then import.** **Preview the import** runs every row through the same checks as the database's own form and lists any that would be skipped, by its row number in Excel. A *Total* line under the records is left out, and a mouse whose ID is already taken (in the colony, or by an earlier row) gets the next free one, with yours kept in its notes; the preview says so for each. **Import 120 mice** (the button counts them) saves the rest as one batch, which **Batch history** can undo; **Change the matches** goes back a step.

6. **A new group, not a sheet?** For mice, **Add many** describes one mouse and how many, or loads the CSV from its **Download a template**. In any inventory and in Plasmids, **Add many** takes a list pasted straight from Excel — one name per line becomes one record each.

7. **Print cage cards** and put them on the cages. From now on, the spreadsheet is the backup, not the record.

### Troubleshooting

#### Rows were skipped on import

The preview lists each one by its row number in Excel and says why. Fix those rows and import just them: importing the whole sheet again would add the other rows a second time.

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/bring-your-lab-in

---

## Import from Excel

Bring in the sheet your lab already keeps, as it is, with no template and no renaming of columns.

Who and where: Anyone who adds records · Every database

1. For mice, make your racks first: **Cages → Rack grid → New rack**, named as in your sheet. A sheet with *Rack* and *Position* columns then puts every cage in its place; anything without a position waits in *Unplaced*.

2. Open the database and press **•••** in the toolbar above its sheet, then **Import from Excel** (for mice, on the **Mice** tab).

3. **Choose a file** (`.xlsx`, CSV or TSV, up to 15 MB and 5,000 rows) and press **Continue**. If the workbook has several sheets, pick one above the matches.

4. Check where each column goes. Each match says why; change any of them. A column BioManager doesn't have becomes a new column in an inventory or organism database (if you may configure it), or goes **Into the notes**; **Leave out** skips it.

5. Give a value for any must-have column your sheet lacks, like the owner: it goes on every row. For plasmids and stock, also whether every row is *Personal* or *Lab common*.

6. Press **Preview the import**. It runs every row through the database's own checks and lists any that would be skipped, by its row number in Excel. **Change the matches** goes back a step.

7. Press the import button, which counts the records (**Import 120 mice**, say).

The rows are saved as one batch, which **Settings → History** can undo. Dates stay as Excel wrote them, and one that can't be read, or a birth date in the future, is left blank and kept in the notes. A mouse whose ID is already taken gets the next free one, with yours kept in its notes.

### Troubleshooting

#### Rows were skipped on import

The preview lists each one by its row number in Excel and says why. Fix those rows and import just them: importing the whole sheet again would add the other rows a second time.

#### An inventory's # doesn't match our IDs

Each record's # follows the order of the rows it came in with. **•••** → **Renumber** gives each the number in its name (*B12* becomes #12), or numbers them in the order of a column ([Samples and orders](https://biomanager.org/guide/samples-and-orders#every-inventory)).

Related: [Bring your lab in](https://biomanager.org/guide/bring-your-lab-in) [Coming from Excel](https://biomanager.org/guide/coming-from-excel) [Undo and history](https://biomanager.org/guide/undo-and-history)

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/import-from-excel

---

## Home

The page that opens each morning: what needs doing today, in three layouts.

Home is where each day starts: only what needs attention, from every database you can see. Choose how it looks with the **Layout** chips at the top (or in **Settings → Appearance & language → Home layout**); the choice is yours alone.

- **Classic**: Cards, built from the databases your lab keeps and laid out in the sidebar's order: your databases as tiles, then *Counts*, a number for each database (mice, tanks, plasmids, vials or plates, open orders, items running low), and each database's own cards. The mouse colony brings *Animals that may need a look* (below), *Mice older than 30 weeks*, *Upcoming weanings* and the *Genotyping queue*; zebrafish the mating tanks to return; Molecular biology *Recent plasmids* (yours first, marked *No sequence* until one is added); and each fly, worm or other animal database a card of its own with what is due in the next two days, so Drosophila and C. elegans are never mixed. *Expiring & low stock*, the *Next 14 days* and *Recent orders* complete it. The button at the top opens the first database in the sidebar.

- **Tracks**: Every dated job on one ruler of days, one track per kind of work, coloured overdue, today, within 3 days or scheduled. Choose 1, 2 or 4 weeks. *Needs you now* and *Busy days* sit beside it. On a phone it becomes a list of days.

- **Freezer**: Your racks seen from above, lit where something is due, with a **Pull list** of the next three days' jobs in walking order, to take into the room. A cage's cap colour shows its owner. A **!** on a cage means two or more cages with living mice are recorded in that position; it shows the latest, and its tooltip names them all.

**Customize**, beside the layout chips, arranges Classic your way: tick the cards you want, drag them (or use the arrows; the double arrow sends a card to the top) into your order, and make any of them *wide*. Four cards start switched off and are there to add: *Your to-dos* (due this week or undated), *Bookings* (instruments booked in the next week), *Recent pages* of your notebook, and *Calculators* (the ones you opened last, then the usual ones). Under the cards, *Counts* lists a number for every database: the first five show until you tick the ones you want. **Back to the usual** puts everything back, after asking. Like the layout, it is yours alone.

On every layout:

- **For you**: Your unread notifications.

- **Getting started**: While you're new, your first steps, each ticked off when it's done. An admin's list sets the lab up — add a rack, bring in your mice, print cage cards, set up your fly database, invite the lab. A member's is their own — find your mice, scan a cage card, request an order, add a plasmid, read this guide. **Hide this list** puts it away.

- **Upcoming weanings**: The same list the calendar shows; each row opens its cage.

### Animals that may need a look

The first card of the mouse colony (or of zebrafish, in a lab without mice) lists the animals whose records suggest someone should look at them. It says what the records show, with the numbers, and never a diagnosis: what to do is yours and your protocol's to decide. Each row opens the animal (or its experiment, or its tank).

- **Losing weight**: A living mouse whose latest weight is 15% or more below its heaviest of the last 30 days (with two weights or more in them), or below its first weight in an experiment that has started: both weights and their days, and the loss. An admin sets the percentage in **Settings → General → Weight loss to flag**.

- **Notes that may need a look**: A mouse, tank or fish whose notes changed in the last 14 days (the change history says when), or a weight taken in that time with a note, that uses one of these words, in any case: hunched, hunching, lethargic, lethargy, moribund, not eating, off food, dehydrated, dehydration, wound, wounds, wounded, ulcer, ulcers, ulcerated, ulceration, weight loss, losing weight, thin, emaciated, labored (laboured) breathing, piloerection, hypothermic, prolapse; 弓背, 消瘦, 精神差, 精神萎靡, 萎靡, 不进食, 拒食, 脱水, 伤口, 溃疡, 呼吸困难, 体重下降, 体重减轻, 濒死, 竖毛, 低体温, 脱垂. The line it is in is shown. A word just after *no*, *not* or *without* (无, 没有, 未, 未见) isn't counted, so *no wound* and 未见溃疡 stay off. It is a word in a note, not a finding.

- **Not weighed in their experiment**: An animal in an active experiment measuring body weight, not weighed for longer than its regimen's weighing days allow, or 7 days when it plans none ([Experiments](https://biomanager.org/guide/experiments#welfare)).

- **Status and experiment disagree**: A mouse whose status is *experiment* while it is in no experiment (once the lab keeps its mouse experiments here), or something else, such as *geno*, while it is in an active one.

A member sees their own animals and the mice of their experiments; **Show the lab’s** shows everyone's. Animal care, facility managers and admins see the lab's, and **Show only yours** narrows it. Each morning the bell also says how many animals may need a look (not the status ones); turn that off in **Settings → Notifications → Animals that may need a look**. Like any card, **Customize** can put it away.

*The Home page*

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/home-page

---

## Working in a sheet

Edit records the way you edit a spreadsheet: click, type, and it saves.

- **Edit in place**: Click a cell and type, or pick from its list. It saves as you go; a note at the bottom says *All changes saved*. If a change can't be saved (say, a required field emptied) the cell turns red and says why.

- **The dot**: The dot beside the number means alive or usable: a living mouse, a vial in use, an open order, a reagent in stock; grey means it isn't. For animals its colour is their age: **blue** young, **green** adult, **red** old (mice: under 8 weeks, 8 to 30, past 30; fish: under 3 months, to 18 months, past 18; a vial or plate: progeny still developing, adults, past its flip or chunk). An expired reagent, chemical, antibody or virus is red too. Point at a dot to see what it means.

- **Scrolling and New**: The page scrolls, not the sheet: its search and buttons stay at the top of the window, its column names under them, and its count at the bottom. **All** under *per page* lists every row. **New**, at the bottom left, adds an empty row at the end of the sheet with its first cell ready to type in. A strain, fish, line, plasmid or order needs a name or a tank first, so there it opens the form.

- **Open a record**: The pencil opens the full record in a dialog, with every field, grouped. New records open the same dialog.

- **Sort, Columns, Export, Print**: **Sort** by any column, or click a heading. Numbers sort as numbers, here and in every list: cage 2 comes before cage 10, and A2 before A10. **Columns** hides what you don't need; drag an edge to resize. **Export** downloads the rows you see as CSV (mice: also Excel and PDF). **Print**, under **•••** at the toolbar's end, gives a clean sheet. Your sort, filters, hidden columns, widths and column order are remembered on that computer.

- **Put the important columns first**: Drag a column's heading left or right; a line shows where it will land. Without a mouse, open **Columns** and use the arrows beside a column (**Move left**, **Move right**). The tick boxes, the number or ID, and the buttons at the end stay where they are. Pasting a block, **Export** and a phone's cards follow the order you set. **Reset column order**, under **Columns**, puts it back. The order you start from is the lab's: an admin sets it under the database's **Configure**, with the arrows beside each column of your own (**Move up**, **Move down**).

- **On a phone**: A sheet becomes one card per row: the number and its buttons on top, then each column by name. **Columns** still hides what you don't need there.

- **If a save is refused**: Say a tank ID is taken: the page tells you why and reopens the form with what you typed, so you fix one field, not all of them.

- **Layouts**: The layouts sit above the sheet, on the left, the same in every database. Where it fits, a sheet also shows as a **Rack grid** or **Box grid**: each tile shows its record's name and position; drag a tile to move it. On a touch screen, press **Move**, tap a tile, then tap where it goes — another tile swaps with it, *Unplaced* takes it out. Orders also show as a **Board**, a column per status: drag a card along.

- **Suggestions**: Text columns suggest what's been typed before, so the lab spells a vendor or a unit one way.

- **What ended long ago**: Mice that died, cages emptied, tubes used up and vials discarded over 90 days ago aren't listed, so a colony with years of history opens quickly. A line at the top says how many; **Show them** lists everything. Search still finds them, and the mouse export includes them.

- **A long sheet**: A sheet of more than 500 entries (an inventory, the mice, cages, litters, fish tanks or vials) opens with its first page, and each other page comes as you turn to it, in a second or so. Search, sorting, the buttons above the sheet and its count still go by every entry. **Export** takes a few seconds for thousands of entries the first time, and **Print** fetches every row first. The **Box grid** comes when you switch to it, and so do the cages' **Cards**, a few seconds for thousands of cages.

### Troubleshooting

#### A cell turned red

That change wasn't saved; the message at the bottom says why (a required field, a date that isn't one).

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/sheets

---

## Many at once

Select many records and change, move or print them in one go.

- **Add many**: For a new group: describe one record and say how many. In inventories and plasmids you can instead paste a list of names, one per line. For mice, say how many females and males, or load a CSV (**Download a template** gives the columns); you then see an editable preview with the numbers that will be assigned. There, **Fill down** copies the cell you're in to every row below (`Ctrl`/`⌘` + `D` too), and nothing is saved until you press **Create**.

- **Import from Excel**: For the sheet you already keep. Every database takes an Excel workbook or CSV, with any columns: you check how they were matched, see a preview of what would be created and which rows would be skipped, then import them as one batch you can undo. See [Bring your lab in](https://biomanager.org/guide/bring-your-lab-in).

- **Select and act**: Tick rows (shift-click selects a range) and a bar rises from the bottom: set a field, move, change owner or status, sac, retire, delete. **Set field** sets any column on them, your own columns included (a date column takes a date, a number column a number). That includes **Source**, where you pick the colony and type the ID once — handy when one mouse gives a dozen samples and each would otherwise be opened in turn. Records you may not change are skipped and counted, never silently changed.

- **Duplicate**: Copies a record as a new one of yours — the next aliquot, or the same order again.

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/many-at-once

---

## Finding things

Search everything from anywhere, and keep pages open as tabs.

- **The search box** above a sheet filters it as you type: an ID, a genotype, a cage, a note.

- **Chips** beside it narrow it: *All*, *Alive*, *Mine*, *Lab common*, a status, *Expiring soon*.

- **Search everything** with `⌘`/`Ctrl` + `K`, from anywhere: mice, cages, litters, experiments, strains, vials, tanks, lines, clutches, plasmids, orders, samples, reagents, chemicals, antibodies, viruses and notebook pages. Names that are, or start with, what you typed come first ("S20" finds the S20 tubes before a note about an S200 column), and a lot or catalogue number typed in full comes before anything that merely contains it. Arrows to move, Enter to open. The search at the top of the window opens it too; in the Mac app that is the magnifying glass beside the window's buttons.

- **Back and forward.** In the Mac app, the arrows after the magnifying glass go back and forward, as `⌘` `[` and `⌘` `]` do; the button before it hides or shows the sidebar (`⌘` `B`). Hidden, the sidebar is a narrow column of its places, each with its name under it.

- **Tabs.** Following a link moves the tab you're in; **+** opens a new tab on your start page (**Settings → Appearance & language → Open on**; Home if none). Drag to reorder, `Alt` (`⌥ Option` on a Mac) + `1`…`9` to jump. They're still there tomorrow, and they are yours: someone else signing in on the same computer gets their own.

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/finding-things

---

## Undo and history

Undo a whole batch of changes from Settings → History, and see in the Audit log who changed what, and when.

**Settings → History** lists the latest, and **See all** opens Batch history: every bulk change — an Add many, a move, a status change on fifty rows, an import — with **Undo**. If someone has edited those records since, BioManager says so and offers **Undo anyway** rather than silently overwriting their work. Everyone sees their own batches; admins see the lab's. Changes an AI assistant proposed and you approved are here too, as one batch each ([AI assistants](https://biomanager.org/guide/ai-assistants)).

The **Audit log** (admins; **Open the audit log** under **Every change** in **Settings → History**) records every create, edit and delete: when, who, which record, and exactly what changed — `genotype: DBH-Cre → ∅`.

### Troubleshooting

#### I made a mistake with a bulk change

**Settings → History** → **Undo**.

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/undo-and-history

---

## Notifications

The bell and what it tells you: your animals moved, orders arriving, @mentions and genotyping reminders, and how to choose them.

The bell at the top shows what happened while you were away: someone moved your animals or vials, picked from your breeders, recorded a genotype on your mice, an order you placed was ordered, arrived or was cancelled, stock of yours [ran low](https://biomanager.org/guide/samples-and-orders#low-stock), someone wrote `@you` in a record's notes (a reagent, an order, a plasmid, a cage) or a notebook comment, and lab news such as being made admin. Admins are told of each new order request. A notice about one record opens that record — an order notice opens the order. A daily note reminds you of pups waiting to be genotyped, and another says how many [animals may need a look](https://biomanager.org/guide/home-page#animals) (losing weight, not weighed in an experiment, a welfare word in their notes): yours, or the lab's for animal care. Choose which kinds you get in **Settings → Notifications**; you're never notified of your own changes.

If your server sends email, a daily digest of what's overdue or coming up — flips, weanings, returns, expiring stock — goes to the email on your profile (**Settings → Notifications → Reminder email**). Clear the email to stop it.

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/notifications

---

## Keyboard shortcuts

Every keyboard shortcut on one page: search with ⌘/Ctrl K, switch tabs, fill down, and the Mac menu bar's keys.

| `⌘`/`Ctrl` `K` | Search everything |
|---|---|
| `Alt` `1`…`9` | Go to tab 1–9. On a Mac, `Alt` is `⌥ Option`, here and below. |
| `Alt` `←` `→` | Previous / next tab (also `Alt` `[` `]`) |
| `Alt` `W` | Close this tab |
| `⌘`/`Ctrl` `B` | Hide or show the sidebar |
| `Esc` | Close a menu or dialog |
| Shift-click | Select a range of rows |
| `⌘`/`Ctrl` `D` | Fill down, in the mice's **Add many** preview |

In the desktop app on a Mac, the menu bar has the usual ones as well:

| `⌘` `T` · `⌘` `W` | New tab · close this tab |
|---|---|
| `⇧` `⌘` `]` `[` | Next / previous tab |
| `⌘` `1`…`9` | Your databases, in the sidebar's order (all of the sidebar is in **Go**) |
| `⌘` `[` `]` · `⇧` `⌘` `H` | Back / forward · Home |
| `⌘` `,` | Settings |
| `⇧` `⌘` `E` · `⌘` `P` | Export this sheet · print |
| `⌘` `R` · `⌘` `=` `-` `0` | Reload · zoom in, out, actual size. **View → Appearance** sets light or dark whatever the system uses. |

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/keyboard-shortcuts

---

## Mouse colony

Mice, cages, litters and breeders, from birth to weaning: racks laid out like yours, and genotyping and weaning dates worked out for you.

### What this does for your week

A colony runs on dates that are easy to get wrong and tedious to keep: when a litter is old enough to genotype, when it must be weaned, which cage is getting crowded, whose mice they are. BioManager's job is to work those out from one thing you already know — the day the pups were born — and then put them in front of whoever is on duty.

| Pups are born | You record the date once ([Record a litter](https://biomanager.org/guide/record-a-litter)). Genotyping and weaning dates are worked out from it and appear on [Home](https://biomanager.org/guide/home-page) and the [calendar](https://biomanager.org/guide/calendar) — the same list in both, so nobody keeps a private one. |
|---|---|
| They are old enough to genotype | The litter becomes one record per pup in a few clicks ([Genotype a litter](https://biomanager.org/guide/genotype-a-litter)), each with its own ear tag and result, instead of a row you retype. |
| Weaning day | [Wean a litter](https://biomanager.org/guide/wean-a-litter) moves the pups into new cages by sex, keeps them attached to the litter they came from, and frees the breeding cage. The cage cards for the new cages print with the genotypes already on them ([Print cage cards](https://biomanager.org/guide/print-cage-cards)). |
| In the animal room | Scan the QR code on a cage card with a phone to open that cage, add a weight or a note with gloves on, and have it in the record before you leave the room ([At the bench](https://biomanager.org/guide/phones-and-cage-cards)). |

What you stop doing: keeping the wean dates in your head or a wall calendar, retyping a litter into a sheet, rewriting cage cards by hand after a wean, and asking whose mouse a cage holds — every record carries its owner, and [who may change it](https://biomanager.org/guide/who-can-do-what).

Tabs across the top: **Mice**, **Cages**, **Litters**, **Breeders**, **Experiments**, **Strains** and **Dropdowns**. The **My colony / My groups / Shared / Everyone** switch changes what you *see*, never what you may edit: *My colony* is yours plus the shared cages you work in, *My groups* your [project groups'](https://biomanager.org/guide/project-groups), *Shared* just the shared cages, *Everyone* every cage. Above the cages, **All**, **Active** (cages with living mice) and a button for each purpose show only those cages. A purpose's button shows its cages that still hold living mice, so past cages stay out of the way; **All** still lists them.

*The mouse sheet*

### Racks and cages

**Cages → Rack grid → New rack**: rows, columns and how positions are labelled — `D7`, `4-7`, `7D` or 1 to 80, like the stickers on your real racks. Cages without a position wait in *Unplaced*; drag them on. An empty cage, with no living mice, isn't listed there; the table still shows it. Each cage has a purpose, an owner, a room and its mice. The purposes:

- **Breeding**: a mating cage, mating now. Only a Breeding cage has **Litter born**, **Genotyping** and **Wean**.

- **Breeder**: the lab's breeding stock, the mice kept to be bred. Each person keeps part of the lab's stock, so a Breeder cage is shared with the lab unless its owner makes it personal, and the **Breeders** tab lists these cages.

- **Experiment**: mice in an experiment.

An admin changes the list under **Configure → Cage purposes** (or the **Dropdowns** tab, the same list), and each purpose added there gets its button above the cages. A cage counts as **Active** while it holds living mice. Select cages to set purpose or owner, move them, or **Retire** the empty ones: each leaves its rack and loses its purpose.

The cages show three ways. **Table**: one row per cage, each with its mice beneath it (edit them in place) and its actions; *Litter born* and *Wean due* come right after the mice, so when to wean is in view. Type over a cage's number to renumber it (its mice go with it; a number another cage has is refused). *Card ID*, right after the number, is the number on the facility's own cage card, if it has one. A cage's mice show the transgene columns the **Mice** tab shows: show or hide *Transgene 3* or *4* there under **Columns**, and the cages follow. **Close all** folds every cage to its row (the page remembers), and **Open all** opens them again; the arrow at the start of a row or its mice count opens or closes one. **Cards**: a card for each cage — where it is, its purpose, owner, strain and when to wean, its mice and the same actions — with its own search and the same buttons, starting on *Active*. **Rack grid**: the racks from the front. The page remembers the one you used last.

*A rack grid*

**Two cages in one position.** A new cage is often set up in a position before the cage there is ended, so a position can hold more than one cage. The cage's form, the sheet, an import or an assistant's proposal puts it there and says which cage with living mice is there already. The rack grid shows the cage put there last (one with living mice before an empty one) and marks the position with **!** while two or more there have living mice. Hover over or tap the **!** to list every cage in that position, and click one to open it, move it or end it. Empty and ended cages don't count. Dragging a cage onto a position still swaps it with the cage shown there.

**Changing a rack's layout.** A cage's place is kept as a row and a column, and the rack's layout gives it its name. So when you change the rows, the columns or how positions are named (**Edit** on the rack grid), cages with living mice or not may get another position name though nobody moved them: swap letters and numbers, and the cage at `F7` would read `G6`. Before saving such a change, BioManager lists every cage it touches, with its position now and after each choice, and asks:

- **Keep each position name** (chosen first when the naming changed): `F7` stays F7 and moves to the cell that is called F7 now.

- **Keep each in the same cell**: the cage stays in its row and column, and its position name changes.

A cage whose name or cell the new layout doesn't have (a smaller rack) stays in the rack with no position, under *Unplaced*, and the dialog counts them, and any position that would hold more than one cage with living mice. **Cancel** saves nothing. Renaming a rack, or making it bigger, asks nothing. The change and the moves are one batch, so **Batch history** can undo them together. Fish racks, fly and worm racks, inventory boxes and plasmid boxes ask the same.

### Mice

- **New mouse** for one, **Add many** for a new group (or a CSV made from its **Download a template**), and **Import from Excel** for the sheet you already keep ([how](https://biomanager.org/guide/bring-your-lab-in)). In Add many, type `new` as the cage to put a group in one new cage; with females and males, each sex gets its own new cage unless you tick *Keep both sexes in one new cage*. In the preview, `new-2`, `new-3`… are further new cages, and a new cage that would hold both sexes is pointed out.

- Each mouse has a **Custom tag**, strain, sex, date of birth (age shown in weeks), status — *breeder, experiment, geno, transfer, sac* — up to four transgenes, a genotype, cage, litter, owner and notes. A date of birth or of death can't be in the future, and a mouse's owner is someone in the lab. The same holds when an [AI assistant](https://biomanager.org/guide/ai-assistants) or a script changes it.

- The number BioManager gives a mouse is its identity: handed out in order, never reused, and what its samples, cage card and experiments all link by. **Custom tag**, beside it, is however the animal itself is marked — an ear tag number, an ear punch such as *RF* or *LB*, a tail tattoo, or your lab's own way. Two mice may carry the same mark, search finds a mouse by it, and a spreadsheet column called *custom tag*, *ear tag*, *notch*, *tattoo* or *tail tattoo* comes into it when you import. Point at a mouse's number and its tag shows there too. If your lab doesn't mark its mice, untick **Custom tag** under **Columns** to hide it.

- **Strain**, after the custom tag, is the mouse's background: *C57BL/6J*, *BALB/cJ*, *129S1/SvImJ*, *FVB/NJ* and the other strains most labs keep are offered as you type, and you can type one of your own. Change the list on the colony's **Dropdowns** tab (Column: *strain*). **Add many** sets one strain for the whole batch, search finds a mouse by it, and a spreadsheet column called *strain* or *background* comes into it when you import.

- Select mice to set a field (owner, status, strain, sex, transgenes, cage, litter, date of birth, date of death, note, or one of your own columns), **Add to experiment**, or **Sac**. A date of birth belongs to the litter: when you select every mouse of a litter, the litter itself takes the new date; mice picked from part of a litter move together into a new litter of that date. Setting sac or a date of death ends the record; it stays in the history.

### Breeding: from litter to weaning

Set up a mating by putting the breeders in a cage whose purpose is **Breeding**. On the **Cages** tab, open it (its arrow or mice count) or find its card under **Cards**: **Litter born**, **Genotyping** and **Wean** are there, and only on Breeding cages. **Create litter** numbers each litter L-1, L-2, L-3… (type your own ID instead if you like).

1. **Litter born** asks for the date of birth (today unless you change it; a date in the future is refused) and, if you know them, the pups, the father and the mother, and records the birth; none of it is required. BioManager works out weaning (P21) and genotyping (P28), or the days set in [Settings → General](https://biomanager.org/guide/lab-setup), which appear on Home and the calendar when due — the same list in both. A cage can have two litters at once (a trio's second female): when it has one not yet weaned, **Litter born** asks whether this is **Another litter**, kept beside the first with its own dates, or **Correct the date** of the first. The cage then lists each litter with its age, and Home and the calendar show each one, with the day it was born.

2. **Genotyping** asks for the mouse numbers of the father and mother, and how many pups were born, filled in from **Litter born** when you gave them there; **Create litter** makes the litter and a mouse for each pup, set to *geno*. They wait in the genotyping queue on Home until you change their **Status** from *geno*; entering a genotype alone doesn't take them off it. With two litters, it asks whose pups, the oldest not yet genotyped first.

3. **Wean** opens *Wean and distribute pups*, already filled with the cage's pups, females and males on separate rows: **Wean and move** sends each row to a new or existing cage, or **Mark weaned, move pups later**. Either way the litter is marked weaned and leaves Home and the calendar. Pups younger than P18 are weaned only after you confirm. With two litters, it asks which, the oldest first; the other stays, with its own weaning date.

**Breeders** lists the Breeder cages, the lab's breeding stock: rack and position, and how many of each sex. Above them, the breeders in Breeder and Breeding cages are counted by genotype, and breeders past 30 weeks are flagged. **Pick** takes a breeder as yours to set up a mating; its owner is notified. A Breeder cage left empty for over 90 days, and a mouse in one that ended that long ago, aren't listed; **Show them** at the top lists them too.

### Experiments, strains, dropdowns

- **Experiments** group mice into a cohort with treatment groups, what is done to them day by day and their body weights: see [Experiments, for every animal](https://biomanager.org/guide/experiments). (The notebook's experiments are the write-ups; these are the animals.)

- **Strains** is the lab's reference list of lines and alleles.

- **Dropdowns** keeps the choices each column offers, so the lab uses the same words. Everyone sees them; only admins change them.

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/mouse-colony

---

## Record a litter

When pups are born in a breeding cage, record the date once and BioManager works out when they are weaned and genotyped.

Who and where: Anyone who may edit the cage · Desktop and lab server

1. In the mouse colony, open the **Cages** tab. Not there? The **My colony / My groups / Shared / Everyone** switch changes which cages you see.

2. Find the breeding cage and open it with the arrow at the start of its row or its mice count, or find its card under **Cards**. **Litter born**, **Genotyping** and **Wean** are only on cages whose purpose is *Breeding*, a mating cage. A *Breeder* cage is the lab's breeding stock and has no litters.

3. Press **Litter born**.

4. Check the **Date of birth**: it is today unless you change it, and a date in the future is refused. **Pups**, **Father** and **Mother** are there too, if you know them; Genotyping fills them in. Every field can be left empty.

5. If the cage has a litter that isn't weaned yet, choose what this one is: **Another litter** (a second female's, a week or two after the first: both are kept) or **Correct the date** (the earlier date was wrong). With two litters there, **Which litter** says whose date you are correcting. Nothing is recorded until you choose.

6. Press **Record the litter**.

BioManager works out weaning (P21) and genotyping (P28), or the days set in [Settings → General](https://biomanager.org/guide/lab-setup), which appear on Home and the calendar when due — the same list in both. In the cage's row, *Litter born* and *Wean due* come right after the mice. Typing a date in *Litter born* there, or in **New cage**, works the same way, and only on a *Breeding* cage: set its purpose first. Clearing the date works on any cage. To make a record for each pup, go on to [Genotype a litter](https://biomanager.org/guide/genotype-a-litter).

> **Two litters in one cage** A trio's second female often gives birth before the first litter is weaned. Record it as **Another litter**: each litter keeps its own weaning and genotyping dates, the cage lists both with their ages, and Home and the calendar show each one, such as *Wean Cage 101 (born Sep 29)*. **Genotyping** and **Wean** then ask which litter, the oldest first.

*A breeding cage, with Litter born, Genotyping and Wean on it*

Related: [Genotype a litter](https://biomanager.org/guide/genotype-a-litter) [Wean a litter](https://biomanager.org/guide/wean-a-litter) [Mouse colony](https://biomanager.org/guide/mouse-colony)

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/record-a-litter

---

## Genotype a litter

Make a mouse for each pup of a new litter, then enter their genotypes when the results come back.

Who and where: Anyone who may edit the cage · Desktop and lab server

1. Once the litter is [recorded](https://biomanager.org/guide/record-a-litter), open the breeding cage on the **Cages** tab and press **Genotyping**.

2. In **Father** and **Mother**, type the parents' mouse numbers, and in **Pups**, how many pups were born. The father, mother and pups you gave at **Litter born** are filled in; otherwise father and mother start as the mouse numbers of the cage's first male and female. Nothing is required: Pups is a whole number from 1 to 40, or left empty to make the litter now and add its pups later.

3. If the cage has two litters, choose whose pups these are under **Litter**. It starts on the oldest litter not yet genotyped.

4. Press **Create litter**. BioManager makes the litter, numbered L-1, L-2, L-3…, and a mouse for each pup, set to *geno*. The pups are in that cage, and they are yours.

5. When the results are in, find the pups: **In the mouse sheet**, on the open cage, lists that cage's mice. On Home, the **Genotyping queue** lists mice waiting, and **View mice** opens the mouse sheet. The genotyping day (P28, or the one set in **Settings → General**) is on Home and the calendar, and a daily note reminds you of pups waiting to be genotyped.

6. Type each pup's result in its **Genotype** cell, and its sex if it isn't set yet. Each cell saves as you type.

7. Change each pup's **Status** from *geno* to what it is for now, such as *breeder* or *experiment*. For many at once, tick them and use **Set field**.

A pup waits in the genotyping queue on Home while its status is *geno*, and leaves it once that changes. If someone else records the genotype of your mice, you are notified.

*Genotyping: the parents, and how many pups to make records for*

Related: [Record a litter](https://biomanager.org/guide/record-a-litter) [Wean a litter](https://biomanager.org/guide/wean-a-litter) [Home](https://biomanager.org/guide/home-page) [Many at once](https://biomanager.org/guide/many-at-once)

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/genotype-a-litter

---

## Wean a litter

At P21, move the pups out of the breeding cage into cages of their own, and the litter leaves Home and the calendar.

Who and where: Anyone who may edit the cage · Desktop and lab server

1. Find the cage: on Home, each row of **Upcoming weanings** opens its cage; or open it on the **Cages** tab, where *Wean due* shows in its row.

2. Press **Wean**. Pups younger than P18 are weaned only after you confirm, with **Wean early**.

3. If the cage has two litters, choose which one under **Litter**: it starts on the oldest, and the rows follow the litter you choose.

4. Check the rows in *Wean and distribute pups*. They start with the cage's pups, females and males on separate rows; the mice in a row go to one place. **Add row** adds another destination. The sex on a row is given to its mice. Mice not listed in any row stay in the cage.

5. For each row, type an **Existing cage**, or leave it empty for a new cage of yours, with **Card (new cage)** as its card's label. A filled *Existing cage* wins over *Card*.

6. Press **Wean and move**. To move the pups yourself later, press **Mark weaned, move pups later** instead.

Either way the litter is marked weaned and leaves Home and the calendar; a second litter in the cage stays, with its own weaning date. Then [print cards](https://biomanager.org/guide/print-cage-cards) for the new cages.

### Troubleshooting

#### I weaned the wrong cage

A weaning is one bulk change: **Settings → History** → **Undo**.

*Wean sits on the breeding cage, beside Litter born*

Related: [Record a litter](https://biomanager.org/guide/record-a-litter) [Genotype a litter](https://biomanager.org/guide/genotype-a-litter) [Print cage cards](https://biomanager.org/guide/print-cage-cards) [Mouse colony](https://biomanager.org/guide/mouse-colony)

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/wean-a-litter

---

## Print cage cards

Print a card for each cage, with a QR code that opens the cage on a phone at the rack.

Who and where: Anyone in the lab · Scanning needs a lab server

1. In the mouse colony, open the **Cages** tab and choose **My colony**, **My groups**, **Shared** or **Everyone**: the cards are for the cages you see. For one cage, the print button on its row or card prints just its card.

2. Press **Cage cards** in the toolbar. For tanks, vials and tubes: **Tank labels** (Zebrafish), **Labels** on a fly or worm database, and **Labels** on ticked samples, reagents or any inventory's rows.

3. Under **Print on**, choose a sheet of cards for any printer, or a label printer's roll: Brother QL (62 × 29, 90 × 29, 100 × 62 mm) or Zebra (2 × 1, 3 × 1, 4 × 2, 4 × 2.5 in). Press **Show**. Your choice is remembered. On a label printer it prints one label a page, typed to fit.

4. Press **Print**. For a label printer, pick it and that label size in the print dialog, with margins **None**.

5. For a Zebra, you can instead press **Download for Zebra (.zpl)**, or **Send to Zebra** once an admin has added its address on the lab's network (under **Send labels straight to a Zebra on the network**).

6. Put each card on its cage.

Each card shows the owner, purpose, where the cage goes (rack and position), its animals with how many of each sex, the genotype and a QR code. Scanning it opens that cage, ready to edit, at the rack.

> **Scanning on a phone** Phones reach a lab server, or a desktop that shares its lab on the network ([Devices](https://biomanager.org/guide/your-data#devices)): otherwise the app on one computer is private to that computer.

### Troubleshooting

#### My phone can't reach the server

Check the address with your admin; that you're on the lab's network, VPN or Tailscale; and, if your lab uses its own certificate, that it's installed on the phone.

*A cage card, as it prints*

Related: [Phones and cage cards](https://biomanager.org/guide/phones-and-cage-cards) [Wean a litter](https://biomanager.org/guide/wean-a-litter) [Mouse colony](https://biomanager.org/guide/mouse-colony)

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/print-cage-cards

---

## Phones and cage cards

Use BioManager on a phone, and print cage cards and labels that open records when scanned.

Who and where: Lab server for phones

- **Android**: Install `BioManager-Android.apk` from the [download page](https://biomanager.org/download) (allow your browser to install apps when asked), type your lab server's address once, and you're in. The **Scan** button reads cage cards. Signed in, the app is one of your devices and keeps the facility on the phone for when there is no signal ([Working offline](https://biomanager.org/guide/phones-and-cage-cards#offline)).

- **iPhone and iPad**: Open the server in **Safari** and tap **Share → Add to Home Screen**. BioManager gets its own icon and opens full screen like an app; your camera scans cage cards. (Android without the app: Chrome → **⋮ → Install app**.)

- **Getting around**: A bar at the bottom holds **Home**, **Calendar**, **Databases** (a list of the lab's databases), **Notebook** and **Scan**, with **Search** in the round button beside it; it shrinks while you read down a page. **Scan** uses the app's scanner, or the phone's camera; in Safari on an iPhone it reminds you to point the **Camera** app at the card, which opens it here. **☰** at the top left brings in the whole sidebar.

- **Working offline**: Animal facilities often have no signal. The Android app and the desktop app keep a copy of what you need there: the colony's racks, cages, mice, litters and recent weights, your to-dos for the next two weeks, fly and worm vials and fish tanks, as you may see them. They refresh it when they open, when the network comes back and every 15 minutes. Before going down, press and hold the **Scan** button and choose **Get ready for the facility** for a fresh copy. When the lab's server can't be reached, the app shows its offline screens instead of an error, marked **Offline** with when the copy was made (amber once it is more than a day old). Find a cage by its ID, card or a mouse's number, or scan its card, and record what you do: **Record a weight**, **Died**, **Move**, a **Note**; on a Breeding cage **Litter born**, **Genotyping** (the pups appear at once, ready to weigh) and **Wean**; tick a to-do; **Flipped** or **Discard** a vial; a note on a tank. Each shows at once, marked **waiting**, and the bar counts the changes waiting. Nothing is lost if the app closes. A Breeding cage lists each litter not yet weaned. With one there, **Litter born** asks whether this is **Another litter** or corrects its date; with two, **Genotyping** and **Wean** ask **Which litter**, the oldest first, as the pages do ([Record a litter](https://biomanager.org/guide/record-a-litter)). Back in signal, the changes go to the lab in the order you made them, each through the same rules as the pages, as you, with the time you did it. If someone changed the same thing meanwhile (marked the mouse Breeder while you marked it dead, recorded another birth date), yours waits under **Needs your decision** in your account menu, and on Home after three days: it shows what you saw, what is there now and who changed it, with **Keep mine**, **Keep theirs** or **Edit**. A different field changed meanwhile is simply kept along with yours. Something the lab refuses (a cage that isn't a Breeding cage any more) is listed on the same page with the reason.

- **Cage cards**: **Cages → Cage cards** prints cards sized for standard card stock — owner, purpose, where it goes (rack and position), animals with how many of each sex, genotype and a QR code. Scanning it opens that cage, ready to edit, at the rack. **Tank labels** (Zebrafish), **Labels** on a fly or worm database, and **Labels** on ticked samples, reagents or any inventory's rows do the same for tanks, vials and tubes.

- **Label printers**: **Print on** chooses a sheet of cards for any printer, or a label printer's roll: Brother QL (62 × 29, 90 × 29, 100 × 62 mm), Zebra (2 × 1, 3 × 1, 4 × 2, 4 × 2.5 in) or cryo-tube labels. It then prints one label a page, typed to fit; in the print dialog pick the label printer and that label size, margins **None**. Your choice is remembered. For tubes, **On each label** chooses what a label says (box, position, lot, owner, a column such as concentration, the day printed), remembered for each database, and **Two lines for long text** wraps a long name or place instead of cutting it. For a Zebra, **Download for Zebra (.zpl)** gives the labels in its own language; or an admin adds the Zebra's address on the lab's network once (under **Send labels straight to a Zebra**), and **Send to Zebra** prints them at once.

> Phones reach a **server** , or a desktop that shares its lab on the network ([Devices](https://biomanager.org/guide/your-data#devices)): otherwise the app on one computer is private to that computer.

*A cage opened on a phone after scanning its card*

*Printable cage cards*

### Troubleshooting

#### My phone can't reach the server

Check the address with your admin; that you're on the lab's network, VPN or Tailscale; and, if your lab uses its own certificate, that it's installed on the phone.

#### The offline screens say "This device has no copy of the lab yet"

The app keeps a copy once you have signed in through it with a signal. Open BioManager once where it reaches the server, signed in, then **Get ready for the facility**.

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/phones-and-cage-cards

---

## Zebrafish

Tanks on racks, fish as groups or individuals, matings and clutches, lines with ZFIN names, and water quality.

### What this does for your week

A fish facility runs on things that go wrong quietly: a mating tank left in overnight, a clutch nobody wrote down, a system whose conductivity drifted a week ago. BioManager keeps those where the whole lab can see them rather than in one person's notebook.

| Setting up a cross | **Set up a mating** records which male and female tanks went in, how many of each, and when they go back. Mating tanks due back show on [Home](https://biomanager.org/guide/home-page) until someone marks them **Returned**, so a fish is not left in overnight because the person who set it up is away. |
|---|---|
| The clutch | **New clutch** records each fertilisation against the cross it came from, so a line's output is a number you can look up instead of a memory. |
| Raising and sorting | Fish live as a group with a headcount until you need them individually, which is how a nursery tank actually works. Select tanks to set purpose or owner, move them, or mark genotyping. |
| The water | **Log reading** keeps temperature, pH and conductivity per system, so when a clutch fails you can look back at the week rather than argue about it. |
| An experiment | A tank's fish or a clutch's larvae go under a treatment as a cohort, following survival, length or a phenotype ([Experiments](https://biomanager.org/guide/experiments)). |

What you stop doing: keeping mating returns on a whiteboard, counting a line's clutches from memory, and discovering a water problem only when the fish tell you.

- **Tanks**: **New tank** or **Add many** (consecutive IDs), on a table or a rack grid. Purposes: stock, breeding, mating, experiment, quarantine. Select tanks to set purpose or owner, move, or mark genotyping. The tank view also has the **Sacrifice log**.

- **Fish**: A group with a headcount, or individuals when you need them; statuses alive, transfer, geno, sac. Move or sac a selection.

- **Clutches**: **Set up a mating**: the male and female tanks, how many of each, and when they go back. Mating tanks due back show on Home until you mark them **Returned**. **New clutch** records each fertilisation.

- **Experiments**: Fish rows, a tank's fish or a clutch's larvae under a treatment, following their survival, length or a phenotype; **New experiment** can start with a tank's fish. See [Experiments](https://biomanager.org/guide/experiments).

- **Lines**: Your line catalogue with ZFIN names and founders.

- **Water**: **Add system** for each recirculating system, and **Log reading** for temperature, pH, conductivity and salinity, with a chart. Tick **Raise an alarm with this reading** to flag a problem.

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/zebrafish

---

## Flies and worms

Vials and plates on racks, with flips that follow the temperature.

### What this does for your week

Fly and worm stocks are lost by missing a flip, and flips depend on the temperature the stock is kept at. BioManager works the schedule out per incubator rather than leaving it to a rota on the wall.

| Where a stock lives | Incubators hold racks or boxes, and each incubator has its temperature — which is what decides how often its vials need flipping. |
|---|---|
| Knowing what is due | **Schedule** shows what is overdue, what is due today, and what is coming in the next week or month. Above each rack, the line says when it was last flipped and when the next is due, red when it has slipped. |
| Doing the flips | Mark a vial **Flipped** (worms: **Chunked**) as you go, a whole rack at a time if that is how you work ([Many at once](https://biomanager.org/guide/many-at-once)). |
| Keeping a line safe | Worms: **New frozen lot** records a freeze, and you thaw one onto a plate when you need it, so a line survives a missed flip. |

What you stop doing: keeping the flip rota on a whiteboard, working out by hand which 25 °C vials are due before the 18 °C ones, and finding out a stock was lost two weeks after it happened.

Drosophila keeps **vials** in racks inside incubators; C. elegans keeps **plates** in boxes. Tabs: the vials or plates, **Schedule**, **Experiments**, **Genotypes**, **Incubators & racks**, **Frozen** (worms) and **Settings**.

1. Under **Incubators & racks**, add each incubator with its temperature, then racks or boxes inside it.

2. **New vial** (or plate): genotype, purpose and position. Fly purposes: stock, experiment, cross, virgins, progeny, expansion, backup. Worm purposes: maintenance, experiment, cross, progeny, synchronized, RNAi, males, starved.

3. **Schedule** shows what's overdue, today and coming up in the next 7, 14 or 30 days. Mark vials **Flipped** (worms: **Chunked**), **Collect eggs** into a new vial (worms: **Pick progeny**), and record scoring. Intervals follow the temperature: set them under **Settings → Temperatures and timing**, and a rack moved from 25 °C to 18 °C changes its schedule by itself.

4. In **Grid**, the line above a rack says when it was last flipped and when the next is due (red when overdue), and **Flipped today** beside Edit records a flip of the whole rack in one click (the rack list under **Incubators & racks** has the same button). Hover over the line for the rule it follows, e.g. *every 14 days at 25 °C*.

5. Worms: **New frozen lot** records a freeze; thaw one onto a new plate when you need it.

**Discard** retires a vial (it can be restored); **Copy to a new vial** starts the next generation. Settings also renames the words and purposes to your lab's.

*Fly vials*

*A fly rack as a grid, with its flip schedule above it*

The **Experiments** tab puts vials or plates under a drug, RNAi or a temperature shift and follows their survival; **New experiment** can start with a rack's vials. See [Experiments](https://biomanager.org/guide/experiments).

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/flies-and-worms

---

## Plants and field crops

Sowings, trays or plots, and the seed you harvest and sow again, a generation at a time.

**Add database** in the sidebar offers two starting points for plants. **Plants** is for pots and trays in growth rooms, growth chambers or a greenhouse, as an Arabidopsis, tobacco or rice lab keeps them. **Field crops** is for plots in a field, raised first in a nursery (a seedbed) and transplanted. Either one is sown and harvested rather than born and dead, and has no sex.

### What it keeps

- **Plants** — one row per plant, or per group of plants with a count. **Sown** is its sowing date, and Age is days after sowing; **Harvested / removed** is filled in when you set its status to *harvested*.

- **Trays** (or **Plots**) — where the plants are, placed on the grid of a growth room, greenhouse or field. A field is a grid of plots, the way a rack is a grid of cages: give it rows and columns, and drag each plot into place.

- **Lines** — each with its background (Col-0, a variety), source and stock number, selection marker, whether it is **Transgenic** and under which **Biosafety permit**, and its **Construct**: the plasmid it was transformed with, chosen from the Plasmids database and linked to it.

- **Sowings** — a batch sown together, with its date, how many were sown, the seed lot it came from, its **Generation** (T2, F3) and its stage: seed, stratifying, seedling, transplanted, flowering, seed set and harvested, or *in the nursery* for a field crop. A sowing in the nursery can sit in the nursery (苗圃) as its place.

- **Crosses** — the two parent lines, when it was pollinated, and when its seed was collected.

- **Environment** — readings for each growth room or field: temperature, humidity, light and day length.

### Seed lots

The **Seeds** tab lists every seed lot, those with seed left first. Each has its line and generation, what it was harvested from, how much was harvested and how much is left (in mg, g, seeds, tubes or packets), where it is kept, its germination and its selection plate.

- **Harvest seed** — the wheat button on a plant, a sowing or a cross opens a new lot already filled in: its line, today's date, and its generation. Seed from a selfed plant is one generation on from the plant (a T1 plant gives T2 seed); seed from a cross is F1. Leave **Mark what it was harvested from as harvested** ticked and the plants are marked harvested and dated, and a cross is marked collected.

- **Sow** — the seedling button on a lot starts a sowing from it, on the Sowings tab. The sowing takes the lot's line and generation, and what you type in **Seed taken** comes off what is left (in the lot's own unit). Counted in seeds, it also fills in how many were sown. A lot can't give more than it has.

- **Harvested from** shows a lot's descent, newest first: the plant it came from, that plant's sowing, the lot that sowing came from, and so on back to the first lot. Click a lot in it to go to that lot.

- **Labels** prints a label for each lot with seed left, for a tube or a packet, with a QR code that opens the lot.

- **New seed lot** is for seed you already have: from a stock centre, a colleague or a drawer.

*The Seeds tab: S-003 is T2 seed from plant P-01, and its selection plate fits 3:1*

### The selection plate

Grow a T2 lot on its selection (kanamycin, hygromycin, Basta) and type how many seedlings were **Resistant** and how many **Sensitive**. The **Selection** column says what the counts mean, by a χ² test at p = 0.05: *fits 3:1, one insertion*; *fits 15:1, two insertions*; *all resistant: homozygous* (from 30 seedlings up); or that they fit neither, or that more need counting to tell. Hover over it for the χ² values.

### The schedule

The **Schedule** counts days after each sowing: move it out of the cold after 3 days, count germination at 7, transplant at 14, harvest at 70 (Arabidopsis under long days). A field crop transplants from the nursery at 30 days, flowers at 90 and is harvested at 120. Stored seed comes up for a germination test every two years. Change any of them under **Configure → Schedule rules** for your species; Home shows what is due.

### In your own words

Everything here is a setting, under **Configure**: what a plant, a tray, a growth room and a sowing are called; the words for the two dates (**Start date is called**, **End date is called**); the **Stages** a sowing goes through; the **Kinds of place** (growth room, greenhouse, nursery, field); the units seed is counted in; and **Young until** and **Old after**, the days that colour the dot before a plant's ID blue (a seedling), then green, then red. Add columns of your own, to plants, trays, lines, sowings, crosses or seed lots, as in [Any other organism](https://biomanager.org/guide/any-organism).

### Troubleshooting

#### The Seeds tab isn't there

Its database was made before seed lots, or without them. Under **Configure**, tick **Seed stocks** and save.

#### A harvest gave the wrong generation

The generation follows the plant's sowing; if that sowing has none, the lot has none either. Type it in the lot, and give the sowing its generation so the next harvest follows on.

#### Sow is greyed out on a lot

The lot is someone else's: taking seed from it changes it, so it follows the same rule as any record. Ask them or an admin, or make a sowing and pick the lot under **Sown from lot** without taking seed.

#### "Only 5 mg left" when sowing

The lot has less seed than **Seed taken**. Check the amount, or correct the lot's **Left** if seed was added to it.

Source: https://biomanager.org/guide/plants

---

## Any other organism

A database for any other organism, described in your own words.

**Add database** in the sidebar builds a database for anything else — Xenopus, axolotls, cell lines, yeast. Start from a mouse-like, zebrafish-like or blank organism and describe it. Plants have starting points of their own, **Plants** and **Field crops**, with seed lots: see [Plants and field crops](https://biomanager.org/guide/plants).

However many you end up with, the sidebar lists them in the order they were added, which is rarely the order you work in. An admin drags them into place right in the sidebar, on any page: hold a database's name, move it up or down, and let go; the new order is saved at once. **All databases → Order in the sidebar** does the same as a list, with a grip to drag or arrows, then **Save the order**. Put the ones you open every day at the top; a database you add later joins the end rather than pushing into the middle of your arrangement. An admin arranges it, and it is the lab's order, the same for everyone.

- **Name and vocabulary** — what to call an animal, its housing (tank, cage, plate), a line, a birth cohort and a breeding event, and whether age is shown in days, weeks, days post-fertilisation, generations or passages (then Age shows the record's own *Passage* or *Generation* column, *P12*). The whole interface then speaks your words.

- **How animals are counted** — individuals, groups with a headcount, or groups with individuals when needed.

- **What it does** — tick what you need: housing and rack positions, lines, crosses and cohorts, pedigree, genotyping, schedules worked out from dates, environment readings, health, weights, a cull log, cryo stocks, seed lots and more. Each has a one-line hint on the page. On the **Schedule**, **Done** takes the day it was really done; each rule counts from its own last Done, so feeding every two days doesn't restart a split due every four.

- **Your own columns** — text, long text, a genotype code, number, date, a choice, yes/no, a lab member, a link to a line, a plasmid from the Plasmids database, or a web link. They are edited in the sheet like the others, and **Set field** sets one on every ticked row.

- **Its own words** — under **Configure**, what its two dates are called (**Start date is called**: Hatched, Sown; **End date is called**), the **Stages** a cohort goes through, and the **Kinds of place** its racks and rooms can be. Leave **Sexes** empty and the Sex column goes. **Young until** and **Old after** (days) colour the dot before an ID: blue while young, green, then red.

- **Who it is for** — *Just me* (a personal database only you and admins see) or *The whole lab*.

**The mouse colony, zebrafish and plasmids take columns of your own too.** Open the database, press **Configure**, and under **Your own columns** add what it doesn't keep yet — an organ weight as a number, a perfusion as a choice of *yes* / *no*, a date, a lab member, a link. Each one appears in that database's sheet and in each record, edited in place like any other cell, and comes along in **Export my data**. Untick *In table* for something you want on the record but not as a column. The arrows beside each (**Move up**, **Move down**) set the order its columns take in the sheet for the whole lab; anyone can still drag the columns of their own sheet into another order. Taking a column away hides it and keeps what your records hold in it, so putting it back shows the values again. Only an admin changes them, because they are the lab's columns, the same for everyone.

A column of your own works like the ones that come with the database: tick rows and **Set field** sets it on all of them at once, **Import from Excel** matches a spreadsheet column to it by name, and search finds a record by what it holds — type the ear-punch code or the batch number into the search box and the records with it come up.

Change any of it later under the database's **Configure**, without losing records. The same page offers inventories (samples, orders, reagents, chemicals, antibodies, viruses, primers & oligos, glycerol stocks, cell lines, a custom list) and fly or worm stock databases. An icon is picked from a grid of the icons themselves; hover over one for its name.

*The Add database page*
